### Observed differences

- Two alternative groups of activities traded share between the windows. In the earlier window, A01, A05, A07 and A09 each ran in about 42–44 in 100 traces, while A03, A11, A12 and A13 each ran in about 57–58 in 100; in the later window the first group each rose to about 52–54 in 100 and the second group each fell to about 47–49 in 100. [OCC001, OCC003, OCC005, OCC007, OCC009, OCC010, OCC011, OCC012]

- The dominant order between the adjacent pair A36 and A37 reversed. Earlier, A37 led to A36 in about 64 in 100 of A37's outgoing transitions and A36 led on to A33 in about 64 in 100; in the later window, A36 led to A37 in about 60 in 100 and A37 led on to A33 in about 58 in 100. Across traces, A36 preceded A37 in about 28 in 100 cases (about 16 before) while A37 preceded A36 fell to about 17 in 100 (about 29 before); the pair stayed immediately consecutive in nearly all joint appearances (about 97 in 100 before, all after), A37's typical position moved slightly later (mean about 0.76 to 0.79 of the trace), and the upstream A32 now hands over to A36 in about 28 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (about 16 before) instead of A37 (about 29 before). [DIR036, DIR037, REL006, LAG002, POS004, DIR032]

- Handovers into A14 shifted within the first group: in the later window A07 led directly to A14 in about 44 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (about 28 before) and A09 in only about 21 in 100 (about 35 before), while A01 passed to A09 in about 37 in 100 (about 26 before) rather than to A07 (about 41 before). A07 and A14 shared traces in about 53 in 100 cases (about 43 before), most often with a one-step gap (about 45 in 100 joint appearances, up from about 28). [DIR001, DIR007, DIR009, REL001, LAG001]

- Repetition around A40 and A41 increased: A40 appeared in about 26 in 100 traces (about 18 before) with about 0.43 occurrences per trace (about 0.31 before), and A41 recurred in about 26 in 100 traces (about 18 before). [OCC034, OCC035]

- Activities executed in every trace (for example A14, A23, A30, A31, A32 and A42) kept full participation in both windows, with occurrence counts differing by no more than about 1 in 100 traces. [OCC013, OCC020, OCC025, OCC026, OCC027, OCC036]

### Inference

Support level: Insufficient evidence

The evidence is insufficient to infer a change in the process. With only 200 traces per window and no screening baseline showing that the number of flagged indicators exceeds what an unchanged process produces, the salient patterns — the opposite share movements of the two activity groups and the reversed order of A36 and A37, each larger than about 90–99 in 100 random re-splits of a stable process — remain compatible with the few chance extremes that comparing roughly 100 activities and activity pairs routinely yields. [OCC001, OCC010, DIR036, DIR037, REL006, LAG002]
